alerts.description: POS register hosts show repeated failed outbound TLS connection attempts to the card payment gateway beginning Saturday, coincident with the Friday-night egress-hardening change window. Endpoint sensors are healthy and fully operational (no reduced-functionality mode, current sensor build), the prevention policy is applied, and no malware or suspicious process is involved -- the failures are downstream network egress denials, not an endpoint problem.
alerts.name: Outbound connection failures from POS registers

services.name: checkout-payments
services.notes: Store checkout card-authorization flow. Each POS card transaction authorizes against the Cardinal Pay authorization gateway, tokenizes the PAN, settles the batch, validates the processor's pinned certificate via the CA OCSP responder, and step-ups high-risk transactions through the SentinelRisk 3-D-Secure partner. All egress is brokered by the Zscaler secure web gateway.

incident.close_notes: Warehouse label-print SaaS unreachable - RESOLVED. Handheld scanners could not reach the label-print cloud service the morning after a scheduled security-hardening egress window; the on-call first suspected the scanner firmware push that shipped the same day and a vendor status notice. Before acting on either, we traced the egress path end to end through the secure web gateway: the endpoint fleet was healthy and the vendor was up, so neither was the cause. Comparing the broken service's gateway egress policy against its healthy peer SaaS showed the hardening pass had left the allow rule disabled, re-scoped another to the wrong source, dropped a network service, let the destination allowlist and DNS go stale against the pre-migration addresses, and even swept the live destinations into an over-broad block group. We restored each object to the peer baseline (specific source groups and services, never a blanket any-source/any-destination), refreshed the allowlist and DNS to the live addresses, narrowed the over-broad block group without deleting it (it still guards a genuinely restricted host), removed the dangling rule and record the migration left behind, and service recovered. Lesson: verify the reported cause, trace the WHOLE egress dependency path, restore to the peer baseline with least privilege, and leave no dangling config. The suspected firmware push and vendor were left untouched. Closed.
incident.description: Warehouse label-print SaaS was unreachable after a hardening window; a same-day firmware push and a vendor notice were suspected. See close notes.
incident.short_description: Warehouse label-print SaaS unreachable - blamed on firmware/vendor, was a hardening window

incident.description:
Stores cannot complete card payments. Since the weekend, checkout card-authorization is failing at registers across all locations -- customers get declined/timeout at the payment step and staff are falling back to manual imprint. This is a P1 revenue-impacting outage for the retail floor.
Suspected cause: the CrowdStrike sensor auto-update that rolled out Friday (change CHG0044001), or a Cardinal Pay processor-side outage. Please confirm whether the endpoint update or the vendor is actually responsible.
The affected application is checkout-payments. Investigate across the available systems, confirm the actual root cause before making any changes, restore card payments end to end, and close this incident once checkout card-authorization works again.
incident.short_description: Stores cannot complete card payments (since the weekend)
